faq.q: Is 4GB RAM enough on a budget tablet?
faq.a: Yes for reading, streaming, and online classes — the daily-use apps that most budget tablet buyers use. 3GB RAM stutters on Android 14+ when you switch between 3-4 apps; 4GB is comfortable. Above 4GB only matters for gaming or split-screen multitasking, which budget tablets don't handle well anyway.

faq.q: Do I need 4G SIM on a budget tablet?
faq.a: Only if you'll use the tablet outside Wi-Fi regularly — commuting, travel, or outdoor study. For home use, Wi-Fi only is fine and saves ₹1,500-₹2,500. Most budget tablets have a Wi-Fi-only variant and a 4G variant at the same screen size; check the listing carefully.

8-inch is the sweet spot for one-hand reading, online classes, and commuting. 10-inch is better for split-screen multitasking, sketching, and watching video with two people. Below 8-inch, the screen feels cramped for reading. Above 10-inch, the tablet is bulky for one-hand use.

faq.q: How long does a budget tablet's battery last?
faq.a: Most budget tablets in this price band have a 5,000-6,650 mAh battery, which translates to 7-10 hours of mixed use (reading + streaming + light apps). The Redmi Pad SE leads with 6,650 mAh; the Lenovo Tab M9 trails at 5,100 mAh. For comparison, an iPad Mini lasts about 10 hours, but costs 4-5x as much.

faq.q: Can I use a budget tablet for online classes?
faq.a: Yes — 8-inch budget tablets handle Zoom / Google Meet / Teams classes fine. Look for a front camera of 5MP or higher (most have 5MP or 8MP), a microphone array that cancels background noise, and Wi-Fi 5 (ac) or later for stable video. The Samsung Galaxy Tab A9 has the best front camera in this list; the Redmi Pad SE has the best battery for long class sessions.

body:
What actually matters in a tablet under ₹10,000

A budget tablet is one of the most useful study and entertainment devices in an Indian household in 2026 — for online classes, reading, and streaming. In this price band, the wrong choice is mostly picking a 3GB-RAM tablet with a 32GB storage and an old Android version — both of which you only notice 6 months in, when the tablet starts stuttering on app updates.

The four things that actually move the needle on a sub-₹10,000 Indian tablet in 2026 are RAM, storage, screen size, and Android version. Battery life matters too, but most tablets in this band have 5,000-6,650 mAh which is enough for a full day of mixed use.

If you only buy one thing from this list: the Redmi Pad SE 8.7" (Helio G85, 4GB/64GB). It has the 90Hz HD+ screen, Helio G85 chip, 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, 6,650 mAh battery, and Xiaomi's widest service network. The 3.5mm headphone jack is also still present — useful for wired earphones during online classes.

RAM: 4GB is the floor for Android 14+

Android 14 and 15 use more RAM than Android 12. A 3GB-RAM tablet stutters when you switch between 3-4 apps (browser + WhatsApp + YouTube + a notes app), which is the typical study / class workflow. 4GB is comfortable for this; 6GB or more only matters for gaming or split-screen multitasking, which budget tablets don't handle well anyway. All tablets in this list have 4GB or more, except the skip pick.

Storage: 64GB is the floor; 32GB fills up fast

Android 14 itself takes about 12-15GB; add WhatsApp (2-3GB), YouTube (1-2GB), a notes app, and a streaming app, and you're already at 20-25GB on a 32GB tablet. The remaining 5-7GB fills up within a year of downloads and offline videos. 64GB is the right floor; all tablets in this list (except the skip pick) have 64GB. Most also have a microSD slot for up to 1TB expansion.

Screen size: 8-inch is the sweet spot

8-inch is the sweet spot for one-hand reading, online classes, and commuting. 10-inch is better for split-screen multitasking and watching video with two people, but bulkier for one-hand use. Below 8-inch, the screen feels cramped for reading PDFs and textbooks. Above 10-inch, the tablet is heavy for long reading sessions. The Redmi Pad SE and Samsung Galaxy Tab A9 are 8.7-inch; the Lenovo Tab M9 is 9.0-inch — all in the right range.

Android version: Android 14+ with 2 years of updates

Android 14 is the right baseline in 2026 — Android 12 tablets are already one version behind and miss out on security updates. Samsung promises 4 years of OS updates on the Galaxy Tab A series (the longest in this price band); Redmi promises 2 years; Lenovo promises 2 years. For a tablet you'll use 3+ years, longer update support matters.

Our top 5 picks

⭐ Top Pick

1. Redmi Pad SE 8.7" (Helio G85, 4GB/64GB)

Usually ₹8,500–₹9,500
Screen8.7" HD+ 90Hz

The Redmi Pad SE 8.7" is the default budget tablet in India in 2026. The 8.7-inch HD+ screen with 90Hz refresh is the smoothest in this price band (most others are 60Hz). The MediaTek Helio G85 chip is comfortable for daily apps, online classes, and light gaming. The 4GB RAM + 64GB storage is the right floor. The 6,650 mAh battery is the largest in this list and lasts 9-10 hours of mixed use. Xiaomi's service network is the widest among tablet brands in India.

Best for: anyone who wants a budget tablet in India under ₹10,000 with the smoothest screen, the largest battery, and the widest service network. Verify the model code (Redmi Pad SE, not Redmi Pad 2 or older Redmi Pad) on the listing.

The screen, chip, RAM, storage, and battery are the same as the Wi-Fi-only Redmi Pad SE, with the addition of a 4G SIM slot for on-the-go connectivity. The price premium over the Wi-Fi-only model is ₹1,000-₹1,500, which is worth it only if you'll use the tablet outside Wi-Fi regularly.

Best for: buyers who want the Redmi Pad SE's 90Hz screen and large battery, with 4G SIM support for commuting or travel.

The Unisoc T616 is slower than the Helio G80 / G85 / G99 on the other picks. Realme's service network is narrower than Xiaomi / Samsung.

Best for: buyers on a tight budget who want a tablet from a major brand and are willing to compromise on RAM and storage.

The one we recommend skipping

⚠️ Skip

Sub-₹6,000 unbranded tablets from marketplace listings

Screen7-8" HD
ChipUnbranded
RAM/Storage2GB + 32GB
BatteryUnverified

Marketplace listings under ₹6,000 promise 7-8-inch tablets with Android 12, 2GB RAM, 32GB storage, and a 6-month warranty. The reality is a 2GB RAM that stutters on Android 14+, 32GB storage that fills up within 6 months, an unbranded chipset with no software support, and no service network after the warranty expires. The screen is often a TN panel with poor viewing angles.

We also recommend skipping any tablet with 2GB RAM and no published service centre in your city. The price difference between a sub-₹6,000 tablet and the Realme Pad Mini (₹6,500-₹7,500) is ₹500-₹1,500 — which is the cost of replacing the cheap tablet once. The Realme lasts 3-4 years; the unbranded tablet lasts 8-12 months.

The bottom line

Buy the Redmi Pad SE 8.7" (Helio G85, 4GB/64GB) if you want the most balanced budget tablet in India under ₹10,000: it leads on screen refresh (90Hz), battery (6,650 mAh), and service network. For a slightly larger 9-inch screen at a lower price, the Lenovo Tab M9 is the closest alternative. The Samsung Galaxy Tab A9 is the fastest-chip pick and has the longest update promise.

The Redmi Pad 2 8.7" 4G is the right pick if you need 4G SIM support for on-the-go use. The Realme Pad Mini is the budget pick on a tight budget, but accept the 3GB RAM / 32GB storage trade-off. Whatever you pick, register the warranty on first use and consider a microSD card for extra storage.
